chunks.text: Bubble Sort repeatedly compares adjacent elements and swaps them if they are out of order. The largest unsorted element 'bubbles' to the end each pass. Worst and average case: O(n^2) comparisons. Best case (already sorted): O(n) if you add an early-exit flag.

Merge Sort divides the list in half, recursively sorts each half, then merges the results. It is O(n log n) in all cases — the divide step produces log n levels, and merging is O(n) per level. It is not in-place: merging requires O(n) extra space.
Linear Search checks each element in order until the target is found or the list is exhausted. Worst case is O(n). It works on unsorted data.

Binary Search requires a sorted list. It compares the target to the middle element: if the target is smaller, search the left half; if larger, search the right half. This is O(log n) because each comparison cuts the remaining search space in half.
